items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I was sort of after the sound of Frankie Trumbauer at that time... I wanted to sound like, I guess, Frankie Trumbauer... The first solo that I copied... was Frankie Trumbauer's 'Singing the Blues'

ctx.x: What happened was, I was playing a C Melody saxophone, which I had bought, and I bought this because that was what I understood Frankie Trumbauer played, and then Willie told me -- Willie "The Lion," that is, said if I was going to play with orchestras, I'd have to have an Alto or a Tenor, because they weren't using C Melodies; you know -- there wasn't any music being written for them in the orchestral parts -- and he was quite right, at that time.

So I got an Alto saxophone, and I'll tell you a very funny thing he used to do to me, which wasn't funny, really; it was very good for me -- but in playing the C Melody saxophone, you are also always playing in the concert key, just

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: that was the first interest that I heard, or the first playing on record that I heard of a saxophone that made me want to play the instrument

ctx.x: The personnel of Gene Goldcat’s band at that time supposedly included Bix Beiderbecke and Frankie Trumbauer. Do you remember seeing him?

That’s strange to me, and it must be true, but I don’t know why I wouldn’t remember Frankie Trumbauer and Bix, but especially Trumbauer, because that was the first interest that I heard, or the first playing on record that I heard of a saxophone that made me want to play the instrument, you know, although I went to the trumpet first, but I guess saxophone was sort of my second interest, and it wasn’t hard for me to change from the trumpet, from the weekend trumpet player that I was.
